clue.text: Birds mating rasp bizarrely

indicators.note: doing something bizarrely means doing it oddly, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Grouse-like birds make a strange rasping cry while courting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptarmigans are mountain grouse, so they are a specific example of birds.

clue.text: Banks are going bust — in a state

indicators.note: something going bust breaks apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Financial collapse grips one American region as its banks fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty US states, a direct example.

clue.text: President frivolous in a tricky situation

parts.note: light can mean frivolous or not serious, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A flippant head of state finds themselves in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or difficult state of affairs, a synonym for a tricky situation.

clue.text: Folk singer participating in live sessions

indicators.note: participating in says the answer takes part inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A folk musician joins some live recording sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Burl Ives was an American folk singer and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Burl Ives was a well-known American folk singer, so the surname fits the description.

clue.text: Nowadays, people of both sexes may put their foot in it

definitions.text: Nowadays, people of both sexes may put their foot in it

parts.words: Nowadays, people of both sexes may put their foot in it
parts.note: putting a foot in it sounds like a social blunder, but literally it is the part of a garment a leg goes into, now worn by women and men alike

explanation.surface: In modern times anyone, man or woman, can say something embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment part that encloses the leg is literally where wearers of either sex put a foot.

clue.text: A second beast turning up in romantic work of art

parts.note: MO, short for moment, means a second

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an otter is a beast, a wild animal

explanation.surface: An animal appears unexpectedly for a moment in a love-themed painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a sculpted or painted cupid, a figure of love in art, hence a romantic artwork.

clue.text: A French company's taken over second international organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second's letter is placed over the company's, sitting above it

parts.note: une is the French for a
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A French business has been bought out by a different global body.
explanation.definitionFit: UNESCO is the United Nations' educational, scientific and cultural body, a worldwide organisation.

clue.text: Knock for six — trick Somerset's tail-ender unleashed!

indicators.note: unleashed means let loose, so that letter is set free from the word

parts.note: a stunt is a trick or daring feat

indicators.note: a tail-ender is the last batsman in cricket, so here the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Somerset cricket batsman at the bottom of the order hits a big shot with a cheeky trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock for six is British slang for stun or shock, from the cricket hit worth six runs. Somerset is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone for six is to shock or overwhelm them, the same as to stun.

clue.text: Oh, excel, fervent Mr Toad — making this lot look silly!

indicators.note: to look silly is to be made a mess of, so these clue letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Toad of Toad Hall boasts of his own brilliance, mocking the learned dons.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Wind in the Willows, Toad sings that the clever men at Oxford know all there is to know, but none know half as much as intelligent Mr Toad. 'this lot' points at those dons.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the Oxford academics whom Toad's boastful song mocks, the group the clue calls this lot.

clue.text: See 9
Start to rouse a man when one hardly ever reacts

indicators.note: start to signals the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Waking a man up is difficult since he barely responds.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble or rare gases such as argon are chemically inert and seldom react, so one fits this description.

clue.text: Rebelled with United Nations force being introduced

indicators.note: being introduced means placed into the other piece

parts.note: to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: People revolted when a United Nations army was brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisen is an old past participle of uprise, to rise up in revolt, hence rebelled.

clue.text: Picture part of collection?

definitions.meaning: an ... is a small picture set within a larger one
something in a set is part of a collection; split as two words

explanation.surface: A painting belonging to an art collection.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small illustration within a page, and split it says belonging to a set.

clue.text: Visitors' accommodation university established — old servant to guard them

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the servant goes around the others

parts.note: a groom was historically a male servant, especially one tending horses

explanation.surface: A college sets up visitor lodging with an old manservant to watch over the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare bedroom kept for visitors to stay in is exactly accommodation for visitors.

clue.text: Incur anger wrecking poet's source of inspiration

indicators.note: wrecking breaks things up, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Getting angry ruins a writer's muse.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote the Ode on a Grecian Urn, so the vase inspired a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient vase prompted Keats's famous ode, making it a poet's inspiration.

clue.text: Miss toying around with a man who can't stand her?

definitions.text: a man who can't stand her?

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman is toyed with by a man who actually dislikes her.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist is someone who hates women, so he cannot stand her.

clue.text: Real tale of war? Different manuscript from this fictional story

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A true war narrative is compared with a novel whose manuscript differs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the answer with MS taken away is an anagram of 'Real tale of war'; that is the same as shuffling those words plus MS. The novel is Hemingway's.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novel is a work of fiction, so it is literally a fictional story.

clue.text: Ronay keeps good works up with something to help the eater

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the critic's name contains the rest

parts.note: Egon Ronay was a famous food critic and restaurant guide writer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OPS, plural of op (opus), are works

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic praises fine dishes that help a diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon for eating a boiled egg is a utensil that helps the eater.

clue.text: Argued about a boy being given appropriate name

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a boy
Ed is a boy's name, fitting for a son

explanation.surface: A dispute arises about a boy being given a suitable name.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoned means argued logically, presenting a case.

clue.text: With this ground condition, hope to get hoe

definitions.text: With this ground condition, hope to get hoe

parts.words: With this ground condition, hope to get hoe
parts.note: a horse-racing going description which, read differently, says the musical soft sign p disappears, turning hope into hoe

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes damp turf will let them use a hoe.
explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) means soft; remove it from hope and you get hoe. The phrase is also a British racecourse going description for yielding turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing reports describe yielding turf with this term, a ground condition.

clue.text: Shy away from bird traversing lake

indicators.note: traversing means stretching across, so the bird spans the other letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird flies across a lake and something recoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to shrink back or shy away from something.

clue.text: Ape rushed into marsh, head disappearing

indicators.note: head disappearing removes the first letter of the result
into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a bog is a marsh
ran means rushed

explanation.surface: A great ape charged into a swamp and sank out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is short for orang-utan, a species of great ape.

clue.text: See 9
Saint having a bit of a snack at home

parts.note: a crisp is a single potato chip, a piece of a snack
in means at home

explanation.surface: A holy figure nibbles a little snack in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a crisp is a thin fried potato slice, what Americans call a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: St Crispin is the patron saint of shoemakers, so the name fits the description.

clue.text: Go through battle without army suffering reverse

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: combat is battle

indicators.note: suffering reverse means being turned backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An army is defeated and withdraws from fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb is to search thoroughly, which means to go through something carefully.

clue.text: What nude's in with nothing on, the fool?

parts.note: a nude person is in the buff, naked
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Asks who is the idiot who appears naked with no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown or ridiculous person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Home abandoned by a German astronomer

indicators.note: abandoned by means left without, so the letter departs

parts.note: an abode is a home

explanation.surface: A German stargazer's house is deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Johann Bode was the German astronomer behind Bode's law of planetary distances.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Elert Bode was an eighteenth-century German astronomer, named directly.

clue.text: Aggressive still on a physicist's scale?

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across clue

parts.note: Mach numbers, named after physicist Ernst Mach, measure speed relative to sound
standing still means speed zero, O

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tough guy registers on a scientist's measuring scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 0 means not moving at all, so still on the Mach scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a showy aggressive masculinity, close to aggressive.

clue.text: Like a nag man's got put off?

definitions.text: Like a nag man's got put off?

parts.words: Like a nag man's got put off?
parts.note: a nag here is a horse, and being put off means being thrown from it, so it has lost its jockey

explanation.surface: A nagging partner has finally driven a man away.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that has thrown its jockey runs with no one on board.
